reference_text:
Welcome to the course. We will work through each concept carefully, connect the
ideas step by step, and use practical examples to make technical topics easier
to understand. When we introduce a new method, focus first on the problem it
solves and why it is useful. For example, in machine learning, features are the
information we give the model, while the target is what we want it to predict.
Now consider a simple question: what changes when the data contains missing
values? We will think through the reason and then look at the code. In Python,
we can inspect the data, run one small step at a time, and explain what the
result means. The goal is to understand the logic, not simply memorize syntax.

slides.title: Cleaning & EDA
slides.transcript:
Welcome to Module 12. Before we trust an analysis or build a model, we need to understand the quality of the data going into it.

Cleaning and exploratory data analysis help us find missing values, duplicates, incorrect types, inconsistent categories, unusual values, and basic patterns.

[tts-break]

The goal is not to make data look perfect. The goal is to understand what is present, what is questionable, and what decisions we are making before analysis.

slides.title: How to use this page
slides.transcript:
For each example, focus on the issue first and the code second.

Ask what could go wrong if the problem is ignored. Then run the code, inspect the result, and think about whether the cleaning decision is appropriate for that context.

[tts-break]

There is rarely one universal cleaning rule. Missing values, duplicates, and outliers all require interpretation, not just syntax.

slides.title: Learning path for Module 12
slides.transcript:
We’ll move through a practical cleaning sequence.

First diagnose the data. Then count missing values, detect duplicates, correct data types, standardize categories, flag possible outliers, and create simple EDA summaries.

[tts-break]

The final example combines those steps into a small cleaning pipeline so you can see how they fit together.

slides.title: Create a messy dataset
slides.transcript:
Let’s begin with intentionally messy data.

Order ID two appears twice. Channel labels use different capitalization and spacing, and one channel is missing. Amount contains numeric-looking text, a missing value, and an unusually large value of nine hundred ninety-nine.

[tts-break]

The dtypes output is also important. Because amount contains strings and missing data, Pandas may not treat the column as a clean numeric type.

This is what real data often looks like before preparation begins.

slides.title: Check missing values
slides.transcript:
The first step with missing data is usually to count it.

Isna dot sum tells us how many missing values appear in each column. Here channel has one missing value and amount has one missing value.

The example fills the missing channel with “unknown” and replaces the missing amount with the median of the available amounts.

[tts-break]

Those are example decisions, not universal rules. In a real project, the correct treatment depends on why the data is missing and how the field will be used.

slides.title: Find duplicate records
slides.transcript:
Duplicates can quietly inflate totals, counts, and frequencies.

Duplicated identifies the repeated row where order ID two and amount seventy-two appear a second time. Drop_duplicates removes the exact duplicate.

[tts-break]

The important question is whether the repetition is truly an error. Two legitimate orders can have the same amount, so we should understand the record definition before deleting anything.

Here the example is intentionally an exact duplicate for teaching purposes.

slides.title: Convert data types
slides.transcript:
Numeric values stored as text need conversion before reliable numerical analysis.

The amount column contains “45”, “72”, “missing”, and “91”. Pd dot to_numeric attempts to convert them. Errors equals coerce turns anything that cannot be converted into NaN instead of raising an exception.

[tts-break]

After conversion, the word “missing” becomes a missing numeric value. That makes the problem visible and lets us handle it using standard missing-data tools.

slides.title: Clean categories
slides.transcript:
Category labels often look different even when they mean the same thing.

Web, space-web-space, EMAIL, email, and Store contain differences in capitalization and whitespace. Str dot strip removes extra spaces, and str dot lower converts everything to lowercase.

[tts-break]

After standardization, web values group together and email values group together correctly.

This kind of cleanup is essential before counting or grouping categories.

slides.title: Flag outliers with IQR
slides.transcript:
The interquartile range, or IQR, gives us one simple rule for flagging unusually large or small values.

We calculate the first quartile, third quartile, and their difference. The upper threshold is Q3 plus one point five times the IQR.

With the current values, nine hundred ninety-nine is far above the rest and should be flagged.

[tts-break]

An outlier flag is not a delete command. Unusual values may be errors, but they may also be important real observations. The next step is investigation.

slides.title: Basic EDA summary
slides.transcript:
Exploratory data analysis gives us a quick picture of the dataset before deeper analysis.

Describe summarizes the numeric amount column with count, mean, standard deviation, quartiles, minimum, and maximum. Value_counts tells us how often each channel appears.

[tts-break]

These simple summaries can reveal skew, unexpected ranges, dominant categories, and other patterns worth investigating.

EDA is about asking better questions before making conclusions.

slides.title: Mini cleaning pipeline
slides.transcript:
Now we combine several cleaning steps in a consistent order.

First, exact duplicates are removed. Missing channel values are filled, then channel text is stripped and converted to lowercase. Amount is converted to numeric, and conversion failures become missing values. Finally, missing amounts are filled with the median.

[tts-break]

Once the table is clean enough for this example, we group by channel and sum the amounts.

The value of a pipeline is consistency: the same ordered steps can be reviewed, reused, and tested.

slides.title: Module 12 wrap-up
slides.transcript:
Let’s summarize the cleaning workflow.

Count missing values before deciding what to do. Check duplicates before calculating totals. Verify data types. Standardize categories before grouping. Flag unusual values instead of automatically deleting them. Use EDA to understand the data before formal analysis or modeling.

[tts-break]

Good analysis starts with knowing what is actually in the dataset.

[tts-break]

In Module 13, we’ll take the cleaned data and focus on evidence and communication. You’ll calculate descriptive statistics, examine distributions, compare groups, look at relationships, discuss uncertainty, and choose visual forms that help explain the findings clearly.
